notes:
Quick, pragmatic SMB lead. Using hosted API for customer support bot + thread summarization.

Problem summary: intermittent latency spikes reported by frontend: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~480-650ms, p99 up to 1.2s when all requests routed to us-west. Client currently sets short timeouts (5s) and surface errors to users. They see more delays during peak hours (US business hours).

What they tried: default region on signup (us-west), small prompt sizes (~100-200 tokens), single-request pattern (no client-side batching). No dedicated caching or prefix caching.

Customer quotes: "We get flashes of slowness — most chats are fine but every few minutes a user times out and complains."

Main asks from call: region guidance (where to point production), recommended timeout settings, prompt length / max_tokens guidance, quick perf tuning checklist they can apply now. Also asked for a sample snippet to set request timeout and region in SDK.

Recommended quick wins we gave on call (SE notes):
- Try routing production traffic to us-east1 for majority of users; us-west appears noisier for their workload.
- Increase client request timeout to 30s for chat endpoints; set streaming fallback to longer socket timeout.
- Reduce model response length by controlling max_tokens and using concise system prompts (target total <= 512 tokens for typical replies).
- Enable per-conversation prefix caching for repetitive system/context to reduce token generation costs and latency.
- Use short-lived retry policy with jitter (3 retries) for transient 5xx/429.
- Quick batch test: run 5 concurrent steady-state clients from us-east and compare p95/p99; SE offered a k6 snippet.

Open items: need to validate p99 after region switch (customer to run A/B), confirm SOC2 artifacts for procurement, AE to send timeout+SDK snippet and region recommendation PRD.
